text: Read the real brand card. Its compact color roles are a shortlist. If their values do not support the inspected ads' treatment, read brand_colors.json … Compare supplied values to the observed artwork and choose the existing token that supports the intended use.
note: Third home of this rule (A1 step 2, A4 brand card note).

text: A body-text role need not become display ink; a page role need not describe every campaign background. Palette tokens are available choices too.

Record a material source/kit difference in the direction: the visible property, selected token/value and whether it preserves the treatment or is a deliberate variation. Token validity does not make a gray field white or a flat fill blurred.
If no supplied choice supports the required treatment, record the kit gap or use an appropriate independently layered image; do not quietly call a compromise a match.
Preserve explicit logo/background restrictions and surface any conflict.

Use the kit's spacing and typography definitions. A token example is not evidence that the token exists. New branded text binds style($type.<role>); do not invent weights, font files or token names. Record missing roles honestly.

token-taxonomy.md, brand-kits.md, modes.md and brand-validation.md own token mechanics and diagnostics. The actual card owns identity definitions. components.md owns logo/image placement; review.md owns visible brand fit.
note: Says review.md owns "visible brand fit" — check whether review.md actually judges brand fit against the brand's look (E4).

text: Token-valid colors still need enough contrast in the actual composition.
